title: What Happened
overview: Tell what happened on a day, a trip or in a storm. Tell it in the right order. Use was, were and more past words: came, told, felt, thought. Say when with before, after, last night and two days ago. Use him, her and them in a story. End a surprise with an exclamation mark.
learningPath: Words: listen, look and say. 25 words.
Patterns: 5 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: a story, the weather and a sign.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen back.
Writing: tell a made-up day, in order.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 16.
In this unit, you tell what happened.
It can be a day, a trip, a party or a storm.
And you tell it in the order it happened.
Listen.
I got up at seven.
I had breakfast.
Then I left.
Now say it in one line.
I got up, had breakfast and left.
Say I one time only.
Put a comma, then and before the last thing.
Every doing word is in the past: got up, had, left.
Not: I got up, have breakfast and leave.
A surprise? Say it with strong feeling.
Write an exclamation mark at the end.
Suddenly, the bus stopped!
My phone! I left it on the train!
Use one exclamation mark, not three.
Now was and were.
Am and is change to was.
I am tired. I was tired.
It is cold. It was cold.
Are changes to were.
We are late. We were late.
There are clouds. There were clouds.
I, he, she and it: was.
You, we and they: were.
More doing words change in the past.
Say them in pairs.
come, came. tell, told.
feel, felt. think, thought.
fall, fell. break, broke.
hear, heard. catch, caught.
In thought and caught, you do not say the g or the h.
Hurt does not change. Hurt, hurt.
Now before and after.
Before lunch, you are hungry.
After lunch, you are not.
I called her after lunch.
We left before the storm.
Then say the time: before work, after lunch. No of, and no to.
Now more time words.
The night before today is last night.
Say last night. Not yesterday night.
Today is Monday. Saturday was two days ago.
Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.
Say at the weekend.
The morning of today, before now, is this morning.
I missed the bus this morning.
Now him, her and them.
In a story, say a name one time.
After that, use a short word.
I saw Dan. I told him.
I met Eva. I called her.
I lost my keys. I found them.
He, she and they come before the doing word.
Him, her and them come after it.
Who got the thing? Say the person first.
I gave him the keys.
In Reading, Eva and Dan go on a trip to the city.
They miss a bus, and then there is a storm!
What happened next? Read and find out.
Now you. Think of a made-up day.
Say three things you did, in order.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

outcomes.outcome: Tell what happened on a day in the right order, with one past word for each thing you did.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 1 practice self-checked; Practice 1 order; Speaking 1 and Speaking 6 recordings; Quiz items 1 and 2.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can say what happened in my day, in order.

outcomes.outcome: Use was and were, and the past words came, told, felt, thought, fell, broke, heard and caught, spelled right.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 2 practice; Practice 2, ten words; Practice 3; Speaking 2 recording; Writing 2 checklist; Quiz items 3 to 5.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write: We were tired. I thought it was Monday.

outcomes.outcome: Say and understand when something happened, with before, after, last night, two days ago and at the weekend.
outcomes.evidence: Patterns 3 and 4 practice; Practice 4; Speaking 3 recording; Reading 2 question 7; Quiz items 6, 8 and 9.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can answer: When did it happen? Two days ago.

outcomes.outcome: Use him, her, it and them in a story, and say who got the thing: I gave him the keys.
outcomes.evidence: Pattern 5 practice; Practice 5; Writing 3 checklist; Reading 1 question 3; Quiz items 10 and 11.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write: I saw her. I gave him the keys.

outcomes.outcome: Understand the details of a short spoken message about what happened, and when.
outcomes.evidence: Speaking 4, five answers checked against the key; Speaking 3, the neighbour's questions answered.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can listen to a message and say what happened.

outcomes.outcome: Read a short story, a weather page and a sign, and find the main point and the details you need.
outcomes.evidence: Reading 1 to 3 questions, ten items; Speaking 5 read-aloud; Quiz item 7.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can read a short story or a sign and find what happened.

outcomes.outcome: Write a short story of a made-up day in order, with a time word, before or after, and one exclamation mark.
outcomes.evidence: Writing 1 and Writing 4 against their checklists; Practice 6, eight items; Quiz item 12; the assignment story.
outcomes.cefrDescriptor: I can write the story of a day, with one exclamation mark.

words.meaning: Come at a time, like a storm or a party. What happened? means: tell me the story.
practice: It happened two days ago.
What happened to your phone? I dropped it.
Happen, happened: just add -ed.
Tell me what happened, in order.
When did it happen? At the weekend.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to ask you What happened? about a made-up day. Answer in two past lines, then check that happened has -ed.

words.meaning: Go down, fast, to the floor.
words.example: The cup fell on the floor.
practice: Fall, fell: it changes.
I fell at the door, but I didn't hurt my leg.
The book fell from the shelf.
Snow fell all night.
Don't stand on the chair. You can fall.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two things that fell in a made-up story. Say fell, not falled, and ask it to check.

words.meaning: Go into parts, or stop working. A glass can break.
words.example: I dropped a glass and it broke.
practice: Break, broke: it changes.
The wind broke a window.
My phone broke. It doesn't work now.
Did you break the cup? No, it fell.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up thing that broke: what it was, and when. Check you said broke, not breaked.

words.meaning: Let a thing fall.
practice: Drop, dropped: two p.
Don't drop the eggs!
She dropped her phone on the bus.
He dropped a cup, but it didn't break.
words.tutor: Type dropped for the tutor and ask it to check the two p. Then say one line about a thing you dropped, real or made up.

words.meaning: Feel bad in a part of you, or make it feel bad.
words.example: I fell, but it didn't hurt.
practice: Hurt, hurt: it is the same in the past.
Are you hurt? No, I'm OK.
The cup fell, but no one was hurt.
My legs hurt after the long walk.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor for three past lines with hurt in them. Check each one: hurt stays hurt in the past, with no -ed.

words.meaning: Be late for a bus or a train. It leaves, and you are not on it.
practice: Miss, missed: two s, then -ed.
Did you miss the train? Yes, I did.
Run! We can't miss the last bus!
She missed the start of the film.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up day when you missed a bus or a train. Say what you did next, with then.

words.meaning: Get on a bus or a train before it leaves.
practice: Catch, caught: it changes.
Can I catch the train at six?
We ran and caught the bus!
She missed the first bus and caught the second one.
words.tutor: Say caught to the tutor five times. The g and the h are quiet. Then use caught in one line about a bus or a train.

words.meaning: Get a sound. You hear music, rain and people.
words.example: I heard the rain on the window.
practice: Hear, heard: it changes.
Did you hear the storm last night?
I can't hear you. Say it again, please.
We heard music in the garden.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor to name a sound. Answer with I heard … and a time word, like I heard the wind last night.

words.meaning: Know how you are inside: happy, tired, cold or hot.
words.example: I felt cold after the rain.
practice: Feel, felt: it changes.
How did you feel after the trip? Tired!
She felt happy at the wedding.
We felt the cold wind on the bridge.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor how you felt after a made-up party, a storm and a long trip. Use felt each time.

words.meaning: Say a thing to a person.
practice: Tell, told: it changes.
He told me the time.
Did you tell her about the party?
I told them a story about the storm.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor a short made-up story in three lines. Then ask it: What did I tell you? Check the order is the same.

words.meaning: Have an idea about a thing. I think it is Monday.
practice: Think, thought: it changes.
I think it is cold today.
We thought the bus was late, but it wasn't.
What did you think of the film?
words.starter: I thought it was …, but it was …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a small mix-up in a made-up day: I thought it was …, but it was … . Check you said thought, with th.

words.meaning: You go to a city, a park or a village for a day or two. Then you come back.
words.example: We went on a trip to the city.
practice: The trip was long, but I liked it.
Did you have a good trip?
One trip, two trips.
Before the trip, I got the tickets.
words.starter: Last month, I went on a trip to …
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up trip in four lines: when, where, one thing that happened and how you felt.

words.meaning: Days with no work and no school. You relax or travel.
words.example: We went on holiday in July.
practice: The holiday was two weeks long.
Where did you go on holiday?
On holiday, I got up late every day.
The weather on holiday was warm.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up holiday. Say on holiday, not in holiday, and use two past words.

words.meaning: A thing that happens and no one wanted it, like a cup that falls and breaks.
practice: I had a small accident: I dropped a cup.
An accident: an, not a.
No one was hurt in the accident.
It was an accident. I didn't see the glass.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a small made-up accident, like a dropped cup. Say sorry, then say what happened, in two lines.

words.meaning: People meet to eat, talk, dance and listen to music.
words.example: The party was at the weekend.
practice: We danced at the party.
Did you go to the party last night?
One party, two parties: the y changes to ies.
I got a present for the party.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up party: when it was, who came and what you ate. Check you said came, not comed.

words.meaning: The day two people get married. There is often a big party.
practice: My cousin's wedding was last year.
We danced at the wedding.
There were a hundred people at the wedding.
Did you go to the wedding? Yes, I did.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up wedding in three lines, with was or were in each. Ask it to check was and were.

words.meaning: How it is outside: hot or cold, sun or rain.
practice: How was the weather on your trip?
The weather is cold today.
We had cold, wet weather at the weekend.
Weather: w-e-a-t-h-e-r.
words.tutor: Ask the tutor How was the weather? for three days. Answer each one with was: It was cold. It was warm.

words.meaning: Water that falls from the clouds.
practice: It rained all night.
Rain, rained: just add -ed.
I had my umbrella in the rain.
Did it rain at the weekend?
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up day with rain. Say the rain once, and it rained once.

words.meaning: Air that moves outside. You can feel it and hear it.
practice: I heard the wind at night.
The wind broke the window.
There was a cold wind on the bridge.
Wind: the i is short, like in sit.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor two things the wind did in a made-up storm. Say both in the past.

words.meaning: It is white and very cold. It falls from the clouds, like rain.
words.example: There was snow on the cars.
practice: It snowed last night.
Snow, snowed: just add -ed.
The snow was white and clean.
Did it snow at the weekend? No, it didn't.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up day with snow. Say there was snow once, and it snowed once.

words.meaning: Very strong wind and rain, at the same time.
words.example: There was a storm last night.
practice: The storm broke a window.
We heard the storm at night.
After the storm, the streets were wet.
Was the storm long? Yes, it was.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about a made-up storm in three lines: before it, in it, after it. Use a past word in each line.

words.meaning: A white or grey thing above you, outside. Rain comes from it.
practice: There was one small white cloud.
The clouds were grey. We took an umbrella.
One cloud, two clouds.
No clouds, no rain.
words.tutor: Think of a day, real or made up. Tell the tutor about the clouds with there was or there were.

words.meaning: Between cold and hot.
words.example: It was warm at the weekend.
practice: The tea was warm, not hot.
The water was warm.
Was it warm on your holiday?
Cold, warm, hot: warm is in the middle.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor about three made-up days: one cold, one warm, one hot. Use was each time.

words.meaning: Very quickly, with no time to think.
practice: We were in the park. Suddenly, it rained!
Suddenly, I heard a sound at the door.
Suddenly: two d, then -ly at the end.
The wind came suddenly.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor a made-up story in three lines. Start line 3 with Suddenly, and end it with an exclamation mark.

words.meaning: One time.
words.example: I went to a wedding once.
practice: It snowed once last month.
I missed the bus once, and I was late.
Once, I lost my keys on a trip.
Once sounds like one, with an s sound at the end.
words.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you did once, true or made up. Start with Once, I … and say it in the past.

grammar.title: In the order it happened: I got up, had breakfast and left
grammar.explanation:
Tell a story in the order it happened.
Put every doing word in the past.
Three things? A comma, then and before the last one.
A surprise? End with an exclamation mark.
grammar.rule:
One thing at a time:
I got up at seven.
Then I had breakfast.
After that, I left.

Or in one sentence:
I got up, had breakfast and left.

Say I one time only.
Every doing word in the past: got up, had, left.

The order is the order it happened.

A surprise or a strong feeling? End with an exclamation mark.
Suddenly, the bus stopped!
My phone! I left it on the train!

One exclamation mark, not three.
Not: It rained!!!
grammar.workedExample:
Put in order: miss the bus, get up late, leave at eight.
1. What happened first? get up late: I got up late.
2. Next? leave at eight: left at eight.
3. Last? miss the bus: missed. Add -ed.
4. One sentence: I got up late, left at eight and missed the bus.
5. It is a surprise, so end with an exclamation mark.
6. Check: three past words? Yes. I one time? Yes.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to go back to now in the middle.
No: I got up, have breakfast and left.
Yes: I got up, had breakfast and left.
Check every doing word. Is it in the past?
grammar.tip: One story, one time: all in the past.
grammar.practice:
Write the past word. Then read the line.
1. I ___ up, had tea and left. (get)
2. We went to the station and ___ the train. (miss)
3. She got up, ___ breakfast and walked to work. (have)
4. They ___ the bus, went to the park and ate lunch. (take)
5. He found his keys, ___ the door and left. (open)
6. End with a full stop or !: My bag! I left it on the bus___
7. End with a full stop or !: I had tea and went to bed___
grammar.answers:
1. got  2. missed  3. had  4. took  5. opened  6. !  7. .
Wrong on 2? Miss ends in s. Just add -ed: missed.
Wrong on 3? Got up and walked are in the past. So have changes to had.
Wrong on 7? It is not a surprise. A full stop is right.

grammar.title: Was and were; came, told, felt, thought
grammar.explanation:
Am and is in the past: was.
Are in the past: were.
More doing words change in the past.
Learn them in pairs: come, came.
grammar.rule:
I am tired. I was tired.
It is cold. It was cold.
We are late. We were late.
They are wet. They were wet.

I, he, she, it: was
you, we, they: were

There is a cloud. There was a cloud.
There are clouds. There were clouds.

Was it cold? Yes, it was. No, it wasn't.
Were you late? Yes, I was. No, I wasn't.

More words that change:
come — came
tell — told
feel — felt
think — thought
fall — fell
break — broke
hear — heard
catch — caught
say — said
hurt — hurt, the same
grammar.workedExample:
It is cold today. Now say it for yesterday.
1. It is one thing, so is changes to was.
2. It was cold yesterday.
Now: They are at a party. Say it for last night.
3. They is more than one person, so are changes to were.
4. They were at a party last night.
5. Check: I, he, she, it: was. You, we, they: were.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to use was every time.
No: They was late. We was tired.
Yes: They were late. We were tired.
It is easy to add -ed to these words too.
No: I thinked. He falled.
Yes: I thought. He fell.
grammar.tip: I was, you were. Come, came. Think, thought.
grammar.practice:
Write was or were, or the past word.
1. The weather ___ warm yesterday.
2. We ___ at a wedding at the weekend.
3. Dan ___ late. He missed the bus.
4. My friends ___ to the party at eight. (come)
5. I ___ the rain on the window. (hear)
6. She ___ tired after the trip. (feel)
7. He ___ me the time. (tell)
8. I ___ it was Monday, but it was Sunday! (think)
grammar.answers:
1. was  2. were  3. was  4. came  5. heard  6. felt  7. told  8. thought
Wrong on 2? We takes were, not was.
Wrong on 8? Think changes: thought. Not thinked.
Wrong on 5? Hear, heard: the d is at the end.

grammar.title: Before work, after lunch
grammar.explanation:
Before and after say when a thing happened.
Put a time or a thing after them: before work, after lunch.
Before lunch, you are hungry. After lunch, you are not.
grammar.rule:
Your day:
seven o'clock: breakfast
one o'clock: lunch
four o'clock: the park

I had breakfast before lunch.
I went to the park after lunch.

before work, before school
after lunch, after dinner
before the storm, after the party
before six o'clock, after ten o'clock

At the start or at the end:
After the storm, we cleaned the street.
We cleaned the street after the storm.
At the start, put a comma after the time.

After that: after the last thing you said.
After lunch: after the time you name.
grammar.workedExample:
Lunch was at one o'clock. Eva called you at three o'clock.
1. The call: three o'clock. Lunch: one o'clock.
2. At three, lunch was finished.
3. So the call came after lunch.
4. Eva called me after lunch.
5. Check: after, then the time word. No of, no to.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to put in one more word.
No: after of lunch. before to work.
Yes: after lunch. before work.
At the start, add a comma: After lunch, we left.
grammar.tip: Before lunch, you are hungry. After lunch, you are not.
grammar.practice:
Dan's Friday:
seven o'clock: got up
eight o'clock: breakfast
one o'clock: lunch
six o'clock: work finished
eight o'clock: a party
Write before or after.
1. Dan got up ___ breakfast.
2. He had lunch ___ breakfast.
3. ___ lunch, he was hungry.
4. He went to the party ___ work.
5. He had breakfast ___ lunch.
6. ___ the party, he was tired but happy.
7. Take out the wrong word: We left after of the party.
grammar.answers:
1. before  2. after  3. Before  4. after  5. before  6. After  7. of: We left after the party.
Wrong on 3? Before lunch, he did not eat for five hours. So he was hungry.
Wrong on 6? The party finished, then he was tired. That is after.

grammar.title: Last night, two days ago, at the weekend
grammar.explanation:
Say the time it happened.
The night before today is last night. Not yesterday night.
Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. Say at the weekend.
grammar.rule:
this morning: today, before now
last night: the night before today
yesterday morning, yesterday afternoon
two days ago: the day before yesterday
at the weekend: on Saturday or Sunday
last weekend: the weekend before this one

Not: yesterday night.
Say: last night.

No in or on before last:
last night. Not: in last night.
Ago comes at the end:
two days ago. Not: ago two days.

At the start or at the end:
Last night, it snowed.
It snowed last night.
grammar.workedExample:
Today is Monday. The party was on Saturday.
1. Sunday is one day before Monday. Saturday is two days before.
2. So: The party was two days ago.
3. Saturday is at the weekend too.
4. So: The party was at the weekend.
5. Check: ago at the end. At before the weekend.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to say yesterday night.
No: I heard the storm yesterday night.
Yes: I heard the storm last night.
Yesterday morning and yesterday afternoon are right.
grammar.practice:
Today is Wednesday. Write the time word.
1. Tuesday night: ___ night
2. Monday: two days ___
3. Saturday and Sunday: ___ the weekend
4. Tuesday morning: ___ morning
5. The morning of today, before now: ___ morning
6. Take out the wrong word: I saw her in last week.
7. Write it right: We met yesterday night.
grammar.answers:
1. last  2. ago  3. at  4. yesterday  5. this  6. in: I saw her last week.  7. We met last night.
Wrong on 1 or 7? Say last night, not yesterday night.
Wrong on 3? Last weekend is right too: the weekend before this one.

grammar.title: Him, her, them: I gave him the keys
grammar.explanation:
In a story, say a name one time.
After that, use him, her, it or them.
They go after the doing word: I saw her. I told him.
grammar.rule:
I: me
you: you
he: him
she: her
it: it
we: us
they: them

I saw Dan. I told him.
I met Eva. I called her.
I lost my keys. I found them.
I dropped the cup. I broke it.

Who got the thing? Say the person first:
I gave him the keys.
She told us the time.
Or say the thing first, then to:
I gave the keys to him.
grammar.workedExample:
Dan was at the door. I gave the keys to Dan.
Make it short.
1. Dan is one man, so: him.
2. The keys are more than one thing, so: them.
3. The person first: I gave him the keys.
4. Or the thing first: I gave them to him.
5. Check: him and them go after the doing word.
grammar.mistake:
It is easy to use he or they after the doing word.
No: I saw he. I called they.
Yes: I saw him. I called them.
He and they come before: He saw me.
grammar.tip: He came. I saw him. They came. I saw them.
grammar.practice:
Write him, her, it, us or them.
1. I met Dan at the party. I told ___ the time.
2. Eva lost her phone. I found ___ on the bus.
3. My friends came late. I saw ___ at the station.
4. Priya called. I gave ___ the address.
5. We missed the train. The driver saw ___ and waited.
Make it short.
6. I gave the tickets to Tomas.
7. She gave a photo to her sister.
grammar.answers:
1. him  2. it  3. them  4. her  5. us  6. I gave him the tickets.  7. She gave her a photo.
Wrong on 3? My friends are more than one person: them.
Wrong on 5? We is you and me. After the doing word, we changes to us.
6 and 7: I gave the tickets to him is right too.

readings.title: A Trip in the Rain
readings.setting: A day trip to the city, told in the order it happened.
readings.passage:
Last Saturday, Eva and Dan went on a trip to the city.
They got up at six, had breakfast and left.
But they were late, and they missed the first bus!
They caught the next one at seven.
The weather was warm, and there were no clouds.
After lunch, they went to the park.
Suddenly, there was a storm!
Dan had an umbrella. He gave it to Eva.
They ran to a café. At the door, Eva fell.
“Are you hurt?” Dan asked her.
“No, I'm OK,” she told him.
In the café, Dan dropped his cup, and it broke!
“Sorry! It was an accident,” he told the man at the desk.
The man was kind. He gave him a new cup of tea.
Before dinner, they caught the train home.
They were wet and tired, but they felt happy.

readings.title: Last Week's Weather
readings.setting: A weather report for a village, written on a Monday.
readings.passage:
Today is Monday. Here is the weather for last week.
Last Monday and Tuesday, it was warm, with no clouds.
On Wednesday morning, there were big grey clouds.
After lunch, it rained for three hours.
On Thursday, there was a storm. The wind was very strong.
People heard it all night.
On Friday, it was very cold. It snowed once, in the evening.
At the weekend, there was snow on every street and car.
Two days ago, on Saturday, people walked in the snow.
Last night, it was cold, but there was no wind.
And today? It is warm again, with no rain!

readings.title: A Sign at the Bus Station
readings.setting: The door of the ticket office at a bus station, the morning after a storm.
readings.passage:
BUS STATION: PLEASE READ
What happened?
Last night, there was a big storm.
At about ten o'clock, the wind broke a window in the ticket office.
No one was hurt.
What now?
The ticket office is closed this morning. You can pay on the bus.
Buses 4 and 9: no buses before twelve o'clock today.
Buses 2 and 7: on time.
Did you miss a bus last night? Give your old ticket to the driver. You can travel today for free.
We are sorry. Thank you!

comprehension.q: What did Eva and Dan miss in the morning?
comprehension.why: Line 3: they were late, and they missed the first bus.

comprehension.q: What happened first: lunch or the storm?
comprehension.a: Lunch. The storm came after lunch.
comprehension.why: Line 6: After lunch, they went to the park. Line 7: Suddenly, there was a storm!

comprehension.q: Line 8 says: He gave it to Eva. What is it?
comprehension.why: Line 8: Dan had an umbrella. He gave it to Eva. It is the umbrella.

comprehension.q: Did Dan want to break the cup?
comprehension.why: Line 13: Dan told the man, “Sorry! It was an accident.”

comprehension.q: How did Eva and Dan feel at the end of the day?
comprehension.why: The last line: They were wet and tired, but they felt happy.

comprehension.a: On Friday evening. It snowed once.
comprehension.why: Line 7: On Friday, it was very cold. It snowed once, in the evening.

comprehension.q: Line 9 says: Two days ago, on Saturday. What day is it today?
comprehension.why: Line 1: Today is Monday. Sunday is one day before. Saturday is two days before.
Line 5: On Thursday, there was a storm. The wind was very strong.

comprehension.q: You need bus 9 at ten o'clock this morning. Can you take it?
comprehension.a: No. There are no number 9 buses before twelve o'clock today.
comprehension.why: The sign says: Buses 4 and 9: no buses before twelve o'clock today.

comprehension.q: You missed a bus last night. What do you do today?
comprehension.a: Give your old ticket to the driver. Then you travel for free.
comprehension.why: The sign says: Give your old ticket to the driver. You can travel today for free.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Got up, had breakfast and left
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each line.
I got up at seven.
I got up, had breakfast and left.
We went to the station and caught the train.
She missed the bus, waited an hour and was late.
Suddenly, it rained!
Tap the mic. Say the 5 lines.
Tap the mic again. Listen.
Check: every doing word in the past?
Check: did you say the last line with strong feeling? It has an exclamation mark.
speaking.tutor: Say the five lines to the tutor. Ask it to tell you any doing word that was not in the past.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Come, came; think, thought
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat. Say each pair.
come, came
tell, told
feel, felt
think, thought
catch, caught
hear, heard
In thought and caught, the g and the h are quiet.
Think and thought start with th, like three.
Now say two lines.
I was tired.
We were late.
Tap the mic. Say the 6 pairs and the 2 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: th at the start of think and thought? No g sound in caught?
speaking.tutor: Say the six past words to the tutor in any order. Ask it which ones it heard, and check them with your list.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — A neighbour asks about your weekend
speaking.instructions:
A neighbour asks about your weekend. Listen. Say your lines.
Neighbour: Hello! How was your weekend?
You: It was good. I went on a trip to ___.
Neighbour: Oh! When did you go?
You: I went ___. (on Saturday, or two days ago)
Neighbour: What happened?
You: First, I ___. Then I ___.
Neighbour: How was the weather?
You: It was ___. There was ___!
Neighbour: How did you feel after it?
You: I felt ___.
Your answers can be made up.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? A time word in line 2? Was in line 4? Felt in line 5?
A friend can read the neighbour's lines. No one with you? Read them, then answer.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
A neighbour asks about your weekend. Listen. Say your lines.
Neighbour: Hello! How was your weekend?
You: It was good. I went on a trip to …
Neighbour: Oh! When did you go?
You: I went … (on Saturday, or two days ago)
Neighbour: What happened?
You: First, I … Then I …
Neighbour: How was the weather?
You: It was … There was …!
Neighbour: How did you feel after it?
You: I felt …
Your answers can be made up.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? A time word in line 2? Was in line 4? Felt in line 5?
A friend can read the neighbour's lines. No one with you? Read them, then answer.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to be your neighbour and ask about your weekend. Answer with a time word each time. Your weekend can be made up.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — A phone message: why I missed the party
speaking.instructions:
Listen to Tomas. He left you a message.
Hi, it's Tomas.
Sorry I missed the party last night!
After work, I went to the station.
I missed the train, and the next one came at nine.
When I arrived, it was ten o'clock and the party was finished.
I saw Priya at the station, and I gave her your present.
She told me it was a good party!
Now answer. Say each answer.
1. When was the party?
2. Why was Tomas late?
3. What time did the next train come?
4. Who got the present?
5. What did Priya tell him?
Tap the mic. Say the 5 answers. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 1. Last night. 2. He missed the train. 3. At nine. 4. Priya. 5. It was a good party.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to leave you a short made-up message about a late train. Then tell it back what happened, in the same order.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Read the storm story with feeling
speaking.instructions:
Go to Reading 1, A Trip in the Rain.
Tap Listen. Follow the words.
Now read it out loud, one line at a time.
At a full stop, stop for a moment.
At an exclamation mark, say the line with strong feeling.
Tap the mic. Read the story, all 16 lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 16 lines? Four lines with strong feeling?
Check: missed, caught, fell and broke, said right?
speaking.tutor: Read the four lines with an exclamation mark to the tutor. Ask it to say them back, and copy its feeling.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Tell a made-up day
speaking.instructions:
Tell the story of a day. A made-up day is fine.
Say 6 lines, in order.
1. Last ___, I went to ___.
2. I got up, ___ and ___.
3. Before ___, I ___.
4. After ___, I met ___. I gave ___ a ___.
5. Suddenly, ___!
6. At the end, I felt ___.
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 6 lines? A time word in line 1?
Check: him, her or them in line 4? Every doing word in the past?
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Tell the story of a day. A made-up day is fine.
Say 6 lines, in order.
1. Last …, I went to …
2. I got up, … and …
3. Before …, I …
4. After …, I met … I gave … a …
5. Suddenly, …!
6. At the end, I felt …
Tap the mic. Say it. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 6 lines? A time word in line 1?
Check: him, her or them in line 4? Every doing word in the past?
speaking.tutor: Tell your six lines to the tutor. Ask it one question: What happened after that? Answer with one more past line.

writing.title: Writing 1 — A morning, in order
writing.prompt:
Write 4 lines about a made-up morning.
Tell it in the order it happened.
Put every doing word in the past.
writing.model:
On Friday, I got up late.
I had a shower, ate an apple and left.
I ran to the station, but I missed the train!
I caught the next one at nine.
writing.criteria:
4 lines, in the order it happened.
Every doing word in the past.
One line with three things: a comma, then and.
One line ends with an exclamation mark.
writing.support:
First, write a list of 4 things.
Like this: get up, have a shower, leave, miss the train.
Next to each one, write the past: got up, had, left, missed.
Then make your 4 lines.
writing.extension: Add a fifth line that starts with Suddenly.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A party or a wedding
writing.prompt:
Write 5 lines about a made-up party or wedding.
Use was in one line and were in one line.
Use came, told, felt and thought.
writing.model:
The wedding was last weekend.
There were a hundred people.
My cousin came from the city.
She told me about her new job.
I felt tired, but I thought it was a beautiful day.
writing.criteria:
5 lines.
Was in one line. Were in one line.
Came, told, felt and thought, each one time.
Spelling: thought is t-h-o-u-g-h-t. Felt has no -ed.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change one or two words in each line.
Check each past word with the list on Pattern 2.
writing.extension: Add a line with heard: I heard music in the garden.

writing.title: Writing 3 — A message: why I was late
writing.prompt:
A friend waited for you, and you were late.
Write a message. Say what happened.
It can be made up. You can use a made-up name.
writing.model:
Hi Ana,
Sorry I was late two days ago.
Before lunch, I lost my keys.
I found them after an hour, in my bag.
Then I missed the bus!
I caught the next one and called you.
See you at the weekend.
Dan
writing.criteria:
5 to 7 lines, and a name at the end.
One time word: last night, two days ago or at the weekend.
Before or after in one line.
Him, her, it or them in one line.
One line ends with an exclamation mark.
writing.support:
Start with the model.
Change the time word, the thing you lost and the bus.
Then check your message. A time word? Before or after? Him or them? One exclamation mark?
writing.extension: Add one line with thought: I thought it was Sunday!

writing.title: Writing 4 — My made-up day out
writing.prompt:
Write a short story about a day out.
It can be a trip, a party or a day with a storm.
Tell it in order. It can be made up.
writing.model:
At the weekend, I went to a party in the village.
Before the party, I got a present for my friend Lena.
I took the bus and arrived at six.
We ate rice and fish, and then we danced.
Suddenly, there was a storm, and the wind broke a window!
We closed the door and played music.
At ten o'clock, I gave her the present.
I got home late, but I felt happy.
writing.criteria:
6 to 8 sentences, in the order it happened.
A time word in the first sentence.
Before or after in one sentence.
Him, her, it or them in one sentence.
One sentence with Suddenly, and one exclamation mark.
Every doing word in the past.
writing.support:
Plan first. Write 6 short notes in order: Saturday, trip, missed the bus, storm, café, tired.
Then make each note one sentence.
Check each sentence with the list.
writing.extension: Add how you felt at the end, and one thing you thought.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Put the morning in order
activities.instructions:
Put the lines in order. Write the letters.
a. After that, I caught the next bus.
b. On Monday morning, I got up late.
c. I arrived at the café at ten. Yara gave me a coffee.
d. I had breakfast and left at nine.
e. I ran to the bus stop, but the bus left!
f. Before lunch, I told her about my morning.
activities.answers:
b, d, e, a, c, f
Look at the start of each line.
On Monday morning starts the story.
After that comes after the bus left.
Before lunch is at the end of the morning.
All 6 in the right place: good. Not all? Read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write the letters on paper. Read the six lines out loud in your order. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Write the past
activities.instructions:
Write the past word.
1. come
2. tell
3. feel
4. think
5. fall
6. break
7. hear
8. catch
9. hurt
10. drop
activities.answers:
1. came  2. told  3. felt  4. thought  5. fell  6. broke  7. heard  8. caught  9. hurt  10. dropped
The hard ones: 4 and 8 have a quiet g and h. 9 does not change. 10 has two p.
9 or 10 right: good. 8 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each word out loud, then its past. Write it. Check each letter with the key.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Was or were?
activities.instructions:
Write was, were, wasn't or weren't.
1. The storm ___ very strong.
2. There ___ big clouds in the morning.
3. ___ you at the party? Yes, I was.
4. My friends ___ late. They missed the train.
5. It ___ warm. There were no clouds.
6. There ___ a hundred people at the wedding.
7. Eva ___ tired after the trip.
8. We ___ at the station. We were at the park.
activities.answers:
1. was  2. were  3. Were  4. were  5. was  6. were  7. was  8. weren't
Check 2 and 6: clouds and people are more than one, so were.
Check 8: the next line says the park, so not the station: weren't.
7 or 8 right: good. 6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud with your word. Write the word. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Before, after, last night
activities.instructions:
Write the right words.
1. I heard the storm (last night / yesterday night).
2. We had a party (at / in) the weekend.
3. She called me two days (before / ago).
4. (After / Ago) lunch, we went to the park.
5. First I had a shower. Then I had dinner. I had a shower (before / after) dinner.
6. It snowed (last / ago) week.
7. I was tired (after / before) the long trip.
8. I missed the bus (this morning / this night).
activities.answers:
1. last night  2. at  3. ago  4. After  5. before  6. last  7. after  8. this morning
Number 8: say this morning, but last night.
7 or 8 right: good. 6 or less: read Patterns 3 and 4 and do it again.
activities.solo: Say each line out loud with your words. Write it. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Him, her, it, them
activities.instructions:
Write one word for the words in ( ): him, her, it, us or them.
1. I saw Dan at the station. I told (Dan) the time.
2. My keys fell. I found (my keys) under the table.
3. Eva was on the bus. I called (Eva) at six.
4. The cup broke. I dropped (the cup).
5. You and I were late. The driver waited for (you and me).
Make it short with him, her or them.
6. I gave the umbrella to Eva.
7. He told the story to his friends.
activities.answers:
1. him  2. them  3. her  4. it  5. us  6. I gave her the umbrella.  7. He told them the story.
Check 5: you and me, after the doing word, is us.
Check 6 and 7: the person first, then the thing.
6 or 7 right: good. 5 or less: read Pattern 5 and do it again.
activities.solo: Write each line with the new word. Read it out loud. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
activities.instructions:
Write . or ? or ! at the end.
1. What happened last night___
2. Suddenly, the wind broke the window___
3. We had lunch after the trip___
4. Oh no, I dropped my phone___
5. Were you at the wedding___
6. It rained on Monday and Tuesday___
7. Help, the box is falling___
8. Did you catch the bus___
activities.answers:
1. ?  2. !  3. .  4. !  5. ?  6. .  7. !  8. ?
A question gets a question mark.
A surprise or a strong feeling gets an exclamation mark.
Lines 3 and 6 get a full stop.
7 or 8 right: good. 6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.solo: Read each line out loud. Is it a question? Is it a surprise? Write the mark. Check with the key.

quizzes.q: I got up, had breakfast and ___ at eight.
quizzes.why: The story is in the past. Every word is in the past: got up, had, left. Leave and leaves are now. Leaving is not a past word.

quizzes.q: Which line is in the right order for a morning?
options: I left, got up and had breakfast.
I had breakfast, left and got up.
I got up, had breakfast and left.
Got up, I had breakfast and left.
quizzes.a: I got up, had breakfast and left.
quizzes.why: First you get up, then breakfast, then you leave. The first two are in the wrong order. The last one needs I at the start.

quizzes.q: They ___ at the party last night.
quizzes.why: They takes were in the past. Was is for I, he, she and it. Are is now, not last night. Be does not go after they here.

quizzes.q: I ___ it was Monday, but it was Sunday!
quizzes.why: Think changes in the past: thought. Thinked adds -ed, and this word does not take -ed. Think and thinks are now.

quizzes.q: Which word is the past of catch?
quizzes.why: Catch, caught: it changes. Catched adds -ed. Cought has the wrong letters: it is a-u-g-h-t. Catch is now.

quizzes.q: Lunch was at one. You called at three. You called ___ lunch.
quizzes.why: Three o'clock comes when lunch is finished, so after. Before is the time up to lunch. Ago goes at the end: two days ago. Last goes with night or week.

quizzes.q: You were late. The bus left, and you were not on it. You ___ the bus.
quizzes.why: Missed: you were late, and the bus left. Caught means you got on it. You drop or break a cup, not a bus.
Say last night. Yesterday night is not right, but yesterday morning is. Last takes no in before it. Ago needs a number: two days ago.
Wednesday is two days before Friday: two days ago. In two days is after now, not before. Ago comes at the end. Last two days is not a time word.

quizzes.q: I saw Dan and gave ___ the keys.
quizzes.why: After the doing word, he changes to him: gave him the keys. He goes before the doing word. His is for a thing he has. Them is for more than one person.

quizzes.q: Eva needed a pen. Which line is right?
quizzes.why: The person first, then the thing: gave her a pen. She goes before the doing word, not after. Not a pen her. Say: a pen to her. Her goes after gave.

quizzes.q: Which line needs an exclamation mark at the end?
quizzes.why: Suddenly means a surprise. End it with an exclamation mark. What happened and Did you hear the storm are questions: question mark. We had lunch at one gets a full stop.

teacherNotes.note: Every card shows one item done before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a short checklist. If you are helping, listen to the recordings together and point at the checklist rather than correcting mid-sentence.

teacherNotes.type: The two errors worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: In a story, learners slip back to the present halfway through: I got up, have breakfast and left. Point at each doing word and ask: now, or then? Let the learner change it. The second is they was and we was, probably because was comes up so often; Practice 3 puts the two side by side. The -ed habit from Unit 10 also produces thinked and falled; Practice 2 is the list to go back to.

teacherNotes.type: Stories are made up, and kept light
teacherNotes.note: No task asks the learner to tell a real bad event. Every story task says a made-up day is fine. The accidents in the unit are a dropped cup, a missed bus and a fall where no one is hurt, and the storm breaks a window with nobody near it. If a learner chooses to tell a real event, follow their lead, but never ask for more.

The source units also taught because and so, the present perfect (Have you ever …?), comparatives and word families; all are later or elsewhere. Did and didn't, -ed and went, had, saw are Unit 10 and are used here with no card. Then and after that were Unit 15; Pattern 3 is before and after with a time word, not with that. The unit says it rained rather than it started to rain, because start plus to is not taught yet.

The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. The learner is told throughout that a made-up day, name and answers are fine. Keep that wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor real personal details.

selfAssessment.statement: I can say what happened in my day, in order.
I can use was and were, and came, told, felt and thought.
I can say when it happened: before lunch, last night, two days ago.
I can write: I saw her. I gave him the keys.
I can listen to a message and say what happened.
I can read a short story or a sign and find what happened.
I can write a short story of a day, with one exclamation mark.

assignment.title: My made-up day out
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Tell a day out in 6 lines, in order. It can be a trip, a party or a day with a storm. Say when it was, use before or after, and say how you felt.
2. Write the story, like Writing 4. Put one exclamation mark in it.
A made-up day is fine. You can use made-up names.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written story
